downside.label: Worker downside
downside.title: The claim pays when worker resources are scarce.
downside.explanation: A public claim that pays in this state can move resources toward workers precisely when their resources are most scarce.

upside.label: Unequal participation in upside
upside.title: Workers gain, but capital-market investors gain more.
upside.explanation: Insurance does not require workers to lose outright. A public claim can also share gains when workers benefit less than the investors who own and price it.

neutral.label: Claim-neutral comparison
neutral.title: Worker and market valuations move together.
neutral.explanation: When worker and investor resources move together, this claim adds no insurance value for the public balance sheet.

none.label: No public risky claim
none.marketed: None of the two modeled risks.
none.role: Borrowing and saving can still move resources over time, but they cannot move resources between different states arriving at the same time.

maintained.label: One public risky claim
maintained.marketed: The combination of risks that changes the claim’s payoff.
maintained.residual: Another combination of risks does not change the claim’s payoff.
maintained.role: Public holdings can provide insurance only along the pattern of risk carried by the traded payoff.

complete.label: Two independent public claims
complete.marketed: Both risks in the local two-risk model.
complete.residual: No modeled risk is left outside the public payoff menu locally.
complete.role: A second independent payoff adds the missing hedge direction. It does not create a free return, give households new trading access, or remove financing limits.

evidenceItems.name: Why a public claim may help workers
evidenceItems.publicWording: A public claim is valuable when it pays in states where an extra public pound matters more for workers than its market price suggests.
evidenceItems.qualification: This is a model mechanism, not a claim that public portfolios always improve welfare or minimize the volatility of worker consumption.

evidenceItems.name: What one traded claim leaves uncovered
evidenceItems.publicWording: With two modeled risks and one risky claim, the government can insure the combination of risks that changes the claim’s payoff. Another combination remains uncovered.
evidenceItems.qualification: This is a local result within the maintained asset menu. It does not establish a global welfare loss or a complete-markets result.

evidenceItems.name: The policy comparison being built
evidenceItems.publicWording: The planned comparison changes the capital-tax rule and the number of public risky claims, always starting from the same economy.
evidenceItems.qualification: The numerical comparison is not yet ready, so this site reports no ranking of instruments or welfare effects.

evidenceItems.name: The measurement programme
evidenceItems.publicWording: The empirical work will measure how automation exposure is related to worker resources, the public budget, and the payoff of candidate public claims.
evidenceItems.qualification: That work is still at the measurement stage. No estimate or causal validation is reported here.
